successors.name: Ulus of Jochi
successors.text: the Cuman steppe east of the Don and the Pontic steppe, assigned to the Ulus of Jochi

ledger.x: 880: the Kimek khaganate forms on the Irtysh and the steppe to the west.
896: the Kimeks hold the Ural-Turgay steppe the Pechenegs had left.
1055: the Kipchaks, called Cumans in the west, meet the Rus'.
1056: the Kipchaks take the Oghuz lands.
1056: the Cumans reach the Pontic steppe east of the Don.
1072: the Kipchak lands reach the south Urals and the Middle Volga.
1138: Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya pass to Atsiz of Khwarazm.
1147: the middle Syr Darya passes to the Qara Khitai.
1210: the lower Syr Darya passes to Khwarezm.
1220: the Irtysh and Altai go to the Mongols.
1227: the Kazakh steppe, the Aral and the Urals pass to the Ulus of Jochi.
1236: Batu's armies attack the western Cuman steppe.
1241: Köten is murdered in Pest and Cuman control of the Pontic steppes ends.
1241: the Cuman steppe passes to the Ulus of Jochi.
1241: the Cuman-Kipchak confederation ceases to exist.

wars.name: Kimek-Pecheneg wars
wars.outcome: The Kimaks take Pecheneg lands on the Syr Darya and in the Aral area and push the Pechenegs toward the Lower Volga (second half of the 9th century).

wars.name: Rus'-Cuman wars
wars.outcome: A war 'lasting 175 years' from the 1061 Cuman invasion of Pereyaslavl: the Cumans beat three sons of Yaroslav at the Alta River (1068), Vladimir Monomakh at the Stugna (1093), were beaten near Lubny (1107), sacked six cities (1177), lost Khan Kobiak (1183)…

wars.name: Cuman wars in the Balkans and Hungary
wars.outcome: Cuman and Pecheneg raids on Adrianople (1078), the Balkans (1086, 1094-1095), Hungary (beaten by Ladislaus I in 1089; Coloman crushed in 1099), and help to the Asen and Peter uprising (1185) and Kaloyan at Adrianople (1205).

wars.name: Kipchak raids on Khwarezm, Volga Bulgaria and Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: The Kimaks sack Khwarezm in 1152 and 1197 and attack Volga Bulgaria in 1183; Kipchaks under Qara Ozan Khan attack Talas in 1181.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Kipchak steppe
wars.outcome: Subutai and Jebe chase the Merkit and Qangli Kipchak allies into northern Kazakhstan (1217 or 1218) without incorporating them; the Mongols defeat the Cumans in Subcaucasia (1220) and fight near the Kalka River (1223); in 1236 they defeat the eastern part of…

certainty.note: Nomad frontiers throughout: no page gives a line.
